title: The wall looked permanent.
paragraphs: The wall looked permanent.

Stone stacked on stone.
Thick. Ancient. Intimidating.
The kind of wall that whispers to every enemy outside it:
“You will never get in.”
That was Jericho.
A fortress city. Military stronghold. Gates sealed. Warriors ready. Towers watching the horizon. To human eyes, Jericho was untouchable.
And standing outside those walls?
Former slaves.
A wandering nation with no siege towers, no battering rams, no elite war machines.
Just a promise from God.
And sometimes the biggest battle is not against the wall…
It’s against the doubt inside your chest.
Because when God gave the battle plan, it didn’t sound like war.

March around the city.
Once a day.
For six days.

No shouting.
No attacking.
No breaking the gates.
Just walking.
Can you imagine what Jericho’s soldiers thought as they watched Israel circle the city in silence?

Mockery.
Confusion.
Arrogant laughter from the towers.
“Is that all they’ve got?”
But heaven was not confused.

Every silent step was an act of faith.
Every lap around the wall was obedience.
Every quiet march was a declaration:
God said this city will fall.
Then came the seventh day.

Seven marches.
Seven trumpets.
One command.
“Shout.”
And when the people lifted their voices in faith…
The earth trembled.
Stone cracked.
Dust exploded into the sky.
The walls of Jericho—walls that looked invincible for generations—collapsed in a moment.
Not because Israel was strong.
But because God had already spoken.
Let that sink deep into your spirit.
The walls didn’t fall because the people shouted.
They shouted because God had already won.
And maybe that’s exactly where you are right now.
Standing in front of a wall.

A wall of addiction.
A wall of fear.
A wall of financial pressure.
A wall of broken relationships.
A wall of shame you’ve been hiding behind for years.
From where you stand, it looks permanent.
Immovable.
Unbreakable.
But the story of Jericho whispers a dangerous truth to every wall you face:
If God has spoken, the wall is already living on borrowed time.
But here is the deeper scandal hidden in the story.
While Jericho was collapsing…
One house was still standing.
Inside that house lived a woman with a past.
Her name was Rahab.

She wasn’t a soldier.
She wasn’t an Israelite.
She wasn’t “religious.”
She was a prostitute in a doomed city.
But she believed.
She believed the God of Israel was real.
So she tied a scarlet cord in her window—the sign of the promise that when judgment came, mercy would find her house.
And when the walls crashed down around the city…
That house remained.
Grace stood where destruction fell.
Rahab and her family were rescued.
And if you follow the story far enough…
You’ll discover something breathtaking.
Rahab becomes part of the lineage of Jesus Christ.
Think about that.
A woman with a scandalous past in a collapsing city becomes part of the family line of the Savior of the world.
Because that’s what God does.
He rescues people the world writes off.
He rewrites stories shame tried to erase.
And that scarlet cord hanging in Rahab’s window?
It points forward to another scarlet thread.
The blood of Jesus.
Because the greatest wall humanity ever faced wasn’t Jericho.
It was the wall of sin separating us from God.

A wall built by pride.
Rebellion.
Secrets.
Failures.
The quiet things we hope no one ever discovers.
No amount of effort could break it.
No religion could climb it.
No good deeds could dismantle it.
So Jesus came.
He stepped into our broken world.
He carried our sin to the cross.
And when He rose from the grave, the greatest wall in history collapsed forever.
Forgiveness opened.
Grace poured out.
And anyone—no matter their past—can walk free.
That means the wall in front of you today is not the end of your story.

Your addiction is not the final chapter.
Your failure is not the final sentence.
Your shame is not the final word.
Because the same God who brought down Jericho is still in the business of collapsing impossible walls.
Sometimes the breakthrough happens suddenly.
Sometimes it comes after six long days of marching.
But obedience is never wasted.
Faith is never invisible to heaven.
And God never forgets His promises.
So if you’re staring at a wall today…
Don’t run.
Don’t surrender.
Don’t believe the lie that it will stand forever.
Keep walking.
Keep trusting.
Keep believing.
And when God says shout…
Shout with faith.
Because the wall may look loud…
But God is greater.

Someone staring at a wall.
Someone fighting a silent battle.
Someone who thinks their story is already over.
Tell them this:

Walls fall.
Grace wins.
Jesus saves.
